The Master of Science in Agricultural Education is designed to prepare graduates for teaching, research, extension, leadership, and administrative positions in the public and private sectors. Students in this master's program focus on a core of agricultural education courses along with an emphasis in educational/training program development, evaluation, teaching/training methods, leadership development, and interpersonal communication.

Step 1: Students in the thesis track will work with their graduate committee to design, propose, and complete a comprehensive, original research project. This is the preferred option for on-campus students in assistantship roles.

Step 2: In coordination with their graduate committee, students in the non-thesis track will complete a comprehensive project or exam. This could be an oral exam and portfolio, journal article, needs assessment, small research project, internship (with objectives), or educational product development.

- Financial aid and scholarships available

**How to Check if Your Transcript Has Been Processed**

- Log in to Raiderlink (opens in new tab): https://www.ttu.edu/it4students/raiderlink.php
- Go to the "MyTech" tab.
- Click on "My Student Dashboard."
- Look for your academic records or transcript status to see if your transcript has been received and processed.

**Additional Tips**
- Processing times may vary, especially during peak periods.
- If you do not see your transcript reflected after several business days, contact your Enrollment Service Specialist for assistance.

**Contact for Help**
- If you have questions or concerns about your transcript status, reach out to your Enrollment Service Specialist. They can provide updates and help resolve any issues.

**Related Resource**
- For more information on submitting transcripts: [TTU Online Transcript Best Practices (PDF)](https://www.depts.ttu.edu/online/advocates-bachelors/TTUOnlineTranscriptBestPractices.pdf)

**Next Step**
- If your transcript does not appear as processed after a reasonable time, contact your Enrollment Service Specialist or email online@ttu.edu for further assistance.

Delivered fully online and asynchronously, the program provides flexibility for working professionals and prepares graduates to excel as accounting practitioners, leaders and strategic contributors in a wide range of organizations.

Developmental Literacy Graduate Certificate

This 15-hour Graduate Certificate in Developmental Literacy fills a need in the community for qualified teachers in developmental reading programs, adult basic education, adult literacy programs, alternative high schools, reading intervention programs in traditional high school settings, and GED programs.

Graduate certificates are intended to meet the supplemental post-baccalaureate education needs of professionals. A graduate certificate program is a set of courses that provides in-depth knowledge in a subject matter. The set of courses provides a coherent knowledge base.

The Developmental Literacy Graduate Certificate is designed for individuals who want to teach adult literacy, adult basic education, G.E.D. preparation, and developmental reading and writing in post-secondary settings. The purpose of the certificate is to give teachers proven methods for closing the literacy “readiness gap” in educational settings such as alternative high schools, adult literacy, adult basic education, G.E.D. preparation, and developmental reading and writing programs.

**Online Raider Teach Educator Preparation Program (Graduate Certificate)**

**Program Overview**
- The Online Raider Teach Educator Preparation Program at Texas Tech University is a high-quality, university-based alternative teaching certification option.
- Designed for individuals who already hold a bachelor’s degree and want to become certified teachers in Texas.
- Earn graduate credit while working toward Texas teacher certification.
- The program is delivered 100% online and is asynchronous, allowing flexibility for working professionals.
- Most coursework can be applied toward a Master’s degree in Curriculum and Instruction or other select graduate programs in the College of Education.

**Prerequisites**
- Bachelor’s degree with a minimum 2.75 GPA.
- State certification has additional requirements, including passing the PACT Exam.

- EDUC 5312: Assessment and Technology in the Classroom
- EDUC 5313: Pedagogy and Professional Responsibilities
